label: AB4C_oC24_20_a_2c_b-001
title: $\alpha$ (low) Cristobalite Structure
comments:
$\alpha$ aluminum and gallium phosphate are closely related to the \href{current_web_home_dir/A2B_tP12_92_b_a-001}{$\alpha$ cristobalite structure of SiO$_{2}$}. 
 The change in symmetry from tetragonal space group $P4_{1}2_{1}2$ \#92 in SiO$_{2}$ to orthorhombic $C222_{1}$ \#20 in AlPO$_{4}$ is caused by the replacement of the silicon atoms by two types of atoms. 
 Near 500K this transforms into the \href{current_web_home_dir/AB12C_cF56_216_a_h_c-001}{$\beta$ cristobalite structure} (Hatch, 1994). 
 For more information, see our \href{current_web_home_dir/Tutorials/SiO2_AlPO4}{silica and aluminum phosphate page}. 
 This structure is ``pseudo-tetragonal,'' with $a = b$, but the presence of ordered aluminum and phosphorous atoms reduces the symmetry to orthogonal. 
 The AFLOW label convention rotates the system by 90$^\circ$ about the z-axis and shifts the origin of the z-axis by c/4.  This swaps the (4a) and (4b) Wyckoff positions, placing the aluminum atom on the (4a) site.
